source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 15ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιος Αγάπιος και των συν αυτώ μάρτυρες: Πλήσιος, Ρωμύλος, Τιμόλαος, Αλέξανδρος, Αλέξανδρος (έτερος), Διονύσιος καί Διονύσιος (έτερος)»

attestations.note: The page enumerates the eight and gives each his country: «Ο Αγάπιος ήταν από τη Γάζα της Παλαιστίνης, ο Τιμόλαος από τη Μαύρη Θάλασσα, οι δύο Διονύσιοι από την Τρίπολη της Φοινίκης, ο Ρωμύλος -υποδιάκονος- από τη Λύδδα ή Διόσπολη, ο Πλήσιος και οι δύο Αλέξανδροι από την Αίγυπτο». It puts the martyrdom in the persecution of Diocletian «(284-304)» — the corpus's interval, 284–305, comes from doxologia and stands — before Urbanus, the eparch of Caesarea, and says they all died by beheading. It prints two distichs and an apolytikion that name them. The page has two men of this name in the company, both from Tripoli of Phoenicia, and distinguishes them only by calling the second «έτερος», the other; this folder is the first of the two as the line prints them.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 28.03.2026 (15. март ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Агапије и седморица с њим: Публије, Тимолај, Ромил, два Александра и два Дионисија.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, an enumerated company of eight: the heading names Agapius and then the seven with him, „Публије, Тимолај, Ромил, два Александра и два Дионисија“. It is the same company the Greek and the Romanian already keep in this folder — Caesarea in Palestine, the prince Urban, Diocletian's persecution, eight men, all beheaded — and the Greek line already quoted here names the same seven beside Agapius in the same order but for the first. The Prologue dates the beheading 303, which falls inside the reign this folder already holds; a sourced interval is not narrowed on a reading, so no date was touched. Its own reading of the seven is unlike either other page: it makes them not yet Christians and never baptised with water, baptised instead in their blood, where doxologia makes them six young men already confessing and saint.gr gives each of them a country. That is recorded in the life and not reconciled. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion. **No Serbian name form was stored for this man.** The heading prints the two Alexanders and the two Dionysii only as „два Александра и два Дионисија“ — two of each, in an oblique form, with nothing to tell one from the other — and a nominative singular lifted out of that would be a form this corpus composed rather than one the Prologue printed.

death.note: saint.gr: «Έζησαν και κέρδισαν τα αθάνατα βραβεία, κατά το διωγμό του Διοκλητιανού (284-304) εναντίον της Εκκλησίας». The page gives no year, so the interval is the reign as it prints it; the three folders the corpus already held carry doxologia's 284–305 and are left as they are.
